paper.title: Look Before You Move: Agent-Interface-Aligned Supervision for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
paper.central_claim: Collecting demonstrations by having a privileged teacher select and execute actions through the deployed VLM agent's skill interface (AIDA), with active-vision teacher behaviour, template spatial-reasoning supervision and a shared train/inference harness, yields an 8B VLM student with 71.76% full-task success on 170 held-out OWMM episodes; teacher sensitivity shows active-vision demonstrations improve the student; the sim-trained agent reaches 38% end-to-end on a real robot without further training and the pipeline applies to EmbodiedBench navigation.
paper.claim_scope_note: Simulation OWMM (pre-mapped, known localization, simplified grasp) is the main setting; real robot and EB navigation are extension evidence.

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: a rule-based teacher with privileged simulator state (masks, poses, projected paths, bearings) chooses and executes skills through the student's 5-skill interface; failed and >16-step episodes are dropped (11,740/13,608 succeed, 10,212 kept); deterministic templates add visibility/direction/readiness/progress reasoning; Qwen3-VL-8B is LoRA-SFT'd with the same prompt/history/schema used at inference; privileged inputs are excluded from the prompt. Strongest controlled evidence is Table 2: same base, LoRA, 4-skill interface, annotation and harness; trajectory-relabelled data (152,478 examples) 38.8% vs AIDA teachers at 28,480 examples 46.3 / 65.5 / 69.6% (single training seed, mean of 3 evaluations). Table 1 baselines are copied from OWMM-Agent and their percentages are not multiples of 1/170 (e.g. 21.90% x 170 = 37.2), so they are not same-episode comparisons. Table 3 is a cumulative stack evaluated once, and the main configuration is its best row on the 170 evaluation episodes (training validation disabled). Real robot: 38% end-to-end, no trial count in text. EB: OWMM-trained policy zero-shot in AI2-THOR 0.55 (base 0.02) over 2x60 episodes x 2 runs. Initial view: in scope as harness-student training; teacher-sensitivity claim well supported; headline cross-paper superiority and physical transfer weakly measured; OWMM->EB zero-shot is closed-loop success on a simulator not used for the teacher data.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: EVIDENCE.md transfer clause 1 and 3: the OWMM-trained policy (teacher data built only in OWMM/Habitat) achieves environment-judged closed-loop success 0.55 on EmbodiedBench navigation in AI2-THOR (2x60 episodes x 2 runs, matched interface), i.e. a simulator and task family not used to build its teacher data. The real-robot 38% lacks trial counts and does not independently support transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Under a fixed 8B student, interface and harness (single training seed), demonstrations from teachers acting through the student's skill interface beat trajectory-relabelled data with 5x more examples (69.6% vs 38.8%), and active-vision teacher behaviour accounts for most of the gain (46.3 -> 69.6%); the OWMM-trained student reaches 0.55 zero-shot on EB navigation (base 0.02).
not_supported_as_stated: 71.76% vs 21.90% is a cross-paper, different-denominator comparison, not a controlled superiority result
component attribution of history/reasoning from a cumulative single-run stack
assessment.not_claimed: No reproduction; all results are author reports.

resolutions.reason: The parent's defining condition is a signal derived from the model itself (or a generator) in the absence of ground-truth labels; here supervision comes from a hand-written teacher reading privileged simulator ground truth, i.e. oracle supervision, not a manufactured proxy. PATTERN_PROTOCOL forbids forcing a label on surface similarity (generate + filter).
